**2\. Project Overview (Person 1: Carissa Chen)** 

**What it is** 

Our Hotel Package Logger is an app for hotel front desk agents to log packages that are delivered for guests, easily find them when the guest arrives, and record the pickup with a signature. It exists because many hotels still track packages with handwritten notes, which can lead to illegible entries, mismatched rooms, and lost packages that can cost the hotel money and their reputation. 

**Current status** 

A hotel front desk agent can open a single-page React app, enter a guest’s first and last name, tracking number, carrier, and submit. The form sends that data to POST /api/packages on a Node.js/Express server, which saves it to MongoDB through Mongoose with the status “Logged”. This path (REQ-1) has two automated Jest tests that run in GitHub Actions on every pull request and are passing on main.  
Everything else is designed in UML (docs/uml/) but not built. These include the search, label scanning, marking a package retrieved, signature pickup, sorting, editing, and staff logging features. The nine open issues (REQ-2 through REQ-10) are the remaining work.

**9\. Architecture: Planned vs. Current (Person 4: \_\_Mehla\_Abebbe\_\_\_\_\_)** 

Every project ends up different from its plan. That is normal. Hiding the difference is the problem. This section makes the difference visible. 

**Two terms you need** 

• **Drift** means the code does something the plan never mentioned. Example: you added a caching layer that is not in the planned diagram. Nothing was violated. The plan is simply out of date. • **Erosion** means the code breaks a rule the plan set. Example: the plan says the front end only talks to the API, but one page now queries the database directly. A boundary was crossed. 

Drift is usually harmless but confusing. Erosion is usually a shortcut that someone will pay for later.

**Common setup problems** 

List any error the new team is likely to hit during setup, and the fix. 

Problem: 

➔ Error: Cannot find module 'express' or missing node modules upon running node server.js. ◆ Fix: Run npm install directly in the project root directory to ensure dependencies are installed. 

➔ Problem: EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::5000. 

◆ Fix: Another instance of the server is running on port 5000\. Kill the process using taskkill /F /IM node.exe (Windows) and restart node server.js.

**13\. Original Team Reflection (Whole team)** 

Answer as a team. Two to four sentences each. 

**What worked well** 

**It was relatively easy to design the project’s user-interface features because the project was straightforward. Planning the UML diagrams, architecture diagram, and wireframes was also manageable because the problem was clearly defined. We based the design on a paper-based logging system and considered the steps an employee would follow to log and deliver a package.** 

**What we would do differently with more time** 

**With more time, we would switch to React Native and further research camera-scanning functionality for package logging. The current application relies on manual entry through a web application, which is less ideal for a fast-paced hotel environment.** 

**Biggest challenge** 

**Our biggest challenge was connecting the frontend to the backend. During manual testing, our requests repeatedly failed, producing error messages indicating that the frontend could not connect to the server.** 

**How close the final product is to the original proposal** 

**The final product implements only one core feature from the original proposal: manually logging packages. Major changes included modifying the technology stack and postponing authentication feature. Additionally, the original UI treated the delivery date and time as optional information, while the current design classifies them as required package information.**
